basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Binds an assignee, an organization, a role or post, a scope and a period into one record.
Differs from a position, which defines the post regardless of who fills it.
Differs from an employment relationship, which holds contract terms and pay.
Differs from a task assignment: it covers a body of work over time, not one work item.

may: Propose an assignment and check eligibility rules.
Resolve who holds which assignment at a given instant.
Detect conflicts such as over-allocation or segregation-of-duties clashes.
Project assignment data to permitted downstream systems.
mustNot: Treat a draft or proposed assignment as effective.
Grant access or authority beyond what the active assignment confers.
Keep using delegated authority after the assignment ends or is suspended.
Override blocking validations without a registered exception.
Disclose protected personal fields to unauthorized consumers.

considerations: Assignment decisions affect workload, pay prospects and wellbeing; allocation should be fair and explained.
Working time and rest limits protect health and must not be bypassed.
Cross-border assignments carry tax, social security and immigration consequences for the worker.
affectedParties: People served by the assigned work

items: An assignment record names assignee, organization unit, role or post, scope and validity period.
Confused with the position, the employment contract, a roster shift and a task.
Lingering access after the assignment ends.
W3C Organization Ontology posts and memberships.
